learnings.title: Research staging must reject duplicate JSON keys and non-finite constants
learnings.claim: Python json.loads accepts repeated object member names by default and keeps the last value; it also accepts NaN and Infinity. Research intake and ledger evidence must reject duplicate keys at any nesting depth and non-finite constants before trusting source or learning identity.
learnings.decision: RESEARCH_STRICT_JSON_IDENTITY_GATE: Decode staged promotions and canonical learning ledger with object_pairs_hook duplicate-key rejection and parse_constant non-finite rejection. Reject ambiguous nested keys before source/learning identity checks; mark the candidate unverified or missing instead of counting it as new, and preserve existing bytes. Require negative tests for nested duplicates and NaN/Infinity, positive valid JSON control, latest PR CI, and main read-back before claiming production integration.
learnings.next_measurement: On existing PR #326 verify tests/test_github_agents.py strict decoder and integration negatives on the latest SHA, then confirm main integration and actual research_learner/report outputs. Do not count pending promotion as canonical learning.
failure_history: 2026-10-26: draft PR #326 staged reporter used plain json.loads; repeated JSON keys and NaN could pass structural validation as a seemingly valid staged candidate.
fallback_history: If strict parser or CI is unavailable, do not promote or count the candidate; preserve existing files and send a SHA-bound handoff through existing bridge_failure #308.
